evidence.quote: In southern Africa flowering is in August–November, and fruiting in November–March.
evidence.doc: PROTA (Plant Resources of Tropical Africa) - Syzygium cordatum, via Pl@ntUse mirror

harvestMonths.notes: PROTA text credited to Brink, M., 2008, PROTA4U record for Syzygium cordatum. SANBI PlantZAfrica (https://pza.sanbi.org/syzygium-cordatum) independently corroborates the flowering half of this: 'It flowers from August to November. The fruits are oval berries, red to dark-purple when ripe.' - but PZA does not itself state a fruit-ripening month, so only the PROTA source is used for the months array.

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: ICRAF Agroforestree Database notes only that 'trees can be grown in containers, in which case they will flower and fruit at an earlier age' (no number given).

chillUnits.notes: Evergreen subtropical/tropical tree; no source explicitly stated a chill requirement or its absence, so left null rather than assuming.

evidence.quote: The flowers provide nectar for honey bees.
evidence.doc: PROTA (Plant Resources of Tropical Africa) - Syzygium cordatum, via Pl@ntUse mirror

pollination.notes: PROTA also describes the flowers as bisexual ('Flowers bisexual, regular, usually 4-merous...') and bee-pollinated, but no source made an explicit self-fertile / needs-cross-pollinator statement, so left null rather than inferring from flower structure alone.

gaps: yearsToFirstCrop / yearsToFullBearing: searched PZA, PROTA (plantuse.plantnet.org) and ICRAF Agroforestree (speciesprofile Spid=1575, apps.worldagroforestry.org/treedb2/AFTPDFS/Syzygium_cordatum.PDF) - no numeric years-to-bearing found in any of the three; only the qualitative container-grown note above.
yieldKgPerTreeMature: no kg/tree figure found in PZA, PROTA or ICRAF Agroforestree pages for this species.
chillUnits: no source discusses chilling requirement for this evergreen indigenous species.
